newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up in holiday shortened session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up in holiday shortened session.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended with modest gains Tuesday in a holiday-shortened session, helped by some light short covering and technical buying ahead of the New Year holiday despite softer cash.
February climbed eight cents to close at $2.757 per million British thermal units. March settled seven cents higher at $2.411. Others ended up by 3.6 to five cents.

"For the most part, we were up on short covering today, but the market took a four day beating before year end, and fundamentally, I think it belongs higher," said one trader, noting light volume and falling open interest on the down move.
NYMEX will be closed Wednesday for the New Year holiday.

The NYMEX spot-February contract slumped 32 percent in the five previouvs sessions and most chartists expected today's technical bounce. But opinions were mixed about where prices were headed from here, with most agreed that weather remains the key.
The National Weather Service's 6-10 day forecast calls for above- to much-above-normal temperatures for the eastern half of the nation, including Texas.

Technically, traders still pegged resistance in February in the $2.82-2.96 gap, with further selling likely at last Thursday's $3.595-3.61 gap and then at the contract high of $4.02. Support remained in the $2.60 area.

In the cash, January Gulf Coast prices were thinly talked Tuesday but notionally down 40 cents to the $2.50 area. Midcon pipes were off about 15 cents to the $2.90 area. January gas in New York firmed 10-20 cents to about $3.60-3.80.
AGA said its weekly gas storage report will be delayed one day until Thursday due to the holiday. Early withdrawal estimates ranged from 110 to 130 billion cubic feet.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 4.9 cents to $2.223. NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas futures did not trade Tuesday.

On the KCBT, February closed up 1.5 cents at $2.48, while deferreds finished 2.5 to 3.5 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 6.5 cents to 27.7 cents (NYMEX premium). ((J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624))
